chunks: Musa ibn al-Qasim, from Abd al-Rahman, from Hammad, from Hariz, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:

It is not objectionable for the Muhrim (one in Ihram) to undergo cupping, provided he does not shave or cut the hair. The correct view is to apply it to the state of necessity, based on the report we narrated from al-Hasan al-Siqill, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him). That report is detailed, and this one is general, so acting upon this one is more appropriate.

key_terms.الْمُحْرِمُ: the person in Ihram (state of consecration for Hajj or Umrah)

ai.seo_question: Is it permissible for a pilgrim in Ihram to undergo cupping?
ai.summary: Shaykh al-Tusi resolves the apparent contradiction between general and specific narrations by restricting the permissibility of cupping for the Muhrim to cases of necessity, thereby preserving the prohibition of hair removal. This methodological approach highlights the Shia scholarly principle of reconciling 'mujmal' (general) and 'mufassal' (detailed) texts to derive precise legal rulings. It underscores the balance between maintaining the sanctity of Ihram rituals and accommodating practical medical needs.
